intuition: Odd and even refer to positions, not stored values. Keep a chain for nodes at positions 1, 3, 5 and another for positions 2, 4, 6. Build both in their original order, then connect the end of the odd chain to the saved start of the even chain.

Keep odd at the current odd-position tail and even at the current even-position tail. Save the initial even node as even_head. The node after even is the next odd node: attach it to odd, then advance odd. The node after the new odd is the next even node: attach it to even, then advance even.

At the end, the odd chain contains positions 1,3,5,... and the even chain contains 2,4,6,..., each in original order. Join the odd tail to the saved even head. The loop requires both even and even.next because only then does another odd node exist.
Reusing pointers preserves node identities and values; overwriting values to mimic the final ordering would not implement the required stable node regrouping.

For [2,4,6,8], one round makes odd point to node 6 and even point to the final node 8. Its next link is None, so the loop stops while even itself remains a node. Joining 6 to even_head=4 produces [2,6,4,8], ending at 8.next=None. By contrast, in the odd-length main example the moving even pointer becomes None after its final rewiring.

steps: For [1,2,3,4,5], initialize odd at node 1, even at node 2, and save even_head=2.
Attach node 3 after odd and advance odd to 3.
Attach node 4 after even and advance even to 4. The two growing chains begin [1,3] and [2,4].
Next attach node 5 to the odd chain. No further even node exists, so even becomes absent.
Join the final odd node 5 to saved even_head 2.
The original nodes now form [1,3,5,2,4], with both positional groups retaining their order.

concept.correctness: Each extension appends the next original odd node to the odd chain and the next original even node to the even chain. Thus both chains keep their original relative orders and contain every node of their position group once. Joining their tails yields exactly the required partition without creating or dropping nodes.
